description:
## Goal

Make the Kernel runtime boundary an ordinary, truthful, private foreign-function boundary.

A public fz wrapper calls a private foreign declaration, which names the physical C export and owns the fz semantic contract. Ordinary resolution retains FunctionId. There is no intrinsic registry, synthetic source, pseudo-extern, name-derived execution path, or reconstructed semantic contract.

## Settled model

- Only `extern "C" defp ...` and `extern "fz" defp ...` are accepted. `extern ... def` is rejected until public FFI policy is deliberately designed.
- Both ABIs call C exports. C passes exactly declared arguments. fz generically prepends current Process* and applies typed representation lanes.
- Private foreign declarations bind lexically and never enter ModuleInterface. Public wrappers retain their own public contracts and docs.
- Declared source name and physical export name match. Rename fz_send_ref, fz_self_raw, fz_make_ref_raw, fz_spawn_ref, and fz_make_resource_ref to their declared names. Delete fz_spawn_opt_ref.
- pid, ref, and cpointer have typed built-in identities. ABI lane selection reads those identities, never rendered type strings.
- spawn/1 remains an ordinary private fz extern plus wrapper. Remove spawn/2 and every spawn_opt path. Do not add other spawn forms here.
- Context-free foreign helpers remain ordinary private C externs only if they name a real export. A fake extern must move to its existing language or IR authority rather than gain a stub or special case.
- A linker symbol is physical ABI data, not semantic authority.

## Physical ABI validation

Retain one runtime-export manifest while user code can privately declare C symbols. It is a physical validation and registration authority only: exact export name, ABI, arity, and wire signature. It never supplies semantic contract, effects, typed result identity, or execution behavior.

fz-5xp.32 owns making that manifest closed after this ticket removes aliases and symbol-keyed execution. This ticket must not weaken current declaration validation or delete the manifest merely to hide a duplicate.

## Strategy

1. Make extern visibility use the existing private FunctionForm and publication path. Convert all runtime-library declarations and executable tests or fixtures to defp, reject public extern syntax, and prove lexical call, private capture, and ModuleInterface exclusion.
2. Prove generic declaration-driven execution on an existing real C export, fz_op_rem_ff, by deleting only its native and interpreter name intercepts and proving interp, JIT, and AOT behavior.
3. Add typed built-in opaque identities and generic ABI lane mapping. Rename truthful direct exports: fz_self reads Process.pid, fz_make_ref is context-free, and fz_make_resource allocates directly in the runtime. Delete the stale MakeResourceHook, ExecCtx.module, JIT thunk, and AOT duplicate.
4. Install one synchronous interpreter scheduler adapter only for fz_spawn and fz_send. It owns typed callbacks through ExecCtx, stores failures in a pending error channel, and checks that channel before decoding an extern return. It never chooses behavior by symbol name or adds boxing.
5. Give Never one generic foreign-call policy before cutting fz_panic: a Never call cannot continue; interpreter faults travel through an explicit context fault channel rather than host abort; native cannot resume if such a call returns. The policy is selected by return representation, never a symbol spelling.
6. Audit every apparent C extern. Relocate fake arithmetic and comparison externs atomically to their existing typed IR operator authority, preserving ordinary Kernel wrapper FunctionIds and captures. Do not manufacture C stubs.
7. Delete spawn_opt, symbol-keyed effect summaries, source aliases, obsolete tests, and only then stale documentation.

## Acceptance

- Private extern source, lexical callable identity, capture behavior, and ModuleInterface visibility use the ordinary function model.
- Generic C calls inject no Process*. Generic fz calls inject exactly one Process* and use declaration-derived typed wire lanes consistently in interpreter, JIT, and AOT.
- A declaration and its physical runtime export have exactly the same name. No _raw or _ref alias and no symbol-keyed execution or effect inference remains.
- Semantic contracts derive from source declarations; the retained runtime manifest validates only physical ABI and registration.
- Self, make_ref, make_resource, spawn, send, and panic agree across doors through direct runtime exports or the one generic scheduler adapter. make_resource has no stale module hook or duplicated engine implementation.
- Never calls have one non-continuation policy and preserve interpreter process errors without terminating the compiler host.
- Context-free real C helpers and relocated language operators agree across doors.
- spawn/2 and all spawn_opt code, hooks, symbols, fixtures, tests, and docs are absent without a compatibility path.
- Equal demand reuses products and unrelated edits do not initiate runtime-boundary work.
- Focused, library, fixture, CLI, check, strict Clippy, format, deterministic reuse, and artifact gates pass. Documentation describes only the retained final model.
- No rejected terminal-descriptor scaffolding, probe, adapter, stale test, or obsolete documentation remains.

## Causality

fz-tfn.69 is complete. This ticket no longer provides a hidden terminal identity to fz-tfn.62; the obsolete dependency is removed. fz-5xp.32 remains blocked by this ticket because it needs final truthful export names before it can close physical ABI validation.

## Review

A fresh ticket-scoped cold review must verify private visibility, declaration and export truthfulness, typed lane selection, exact physical manifest scope, elimination of symbol-keyed execution and effects, generic Never behavior, all-door behavior, spawn_opt deletion, reuse telemetry, documentation, and the one-ticket PR boundary before commit and close.
title: Make Kernel runtime calls ordinary private foreign declarations
